text:
alex: heads-up — after the autotune rollout this morning we're seeing a p95 latency spike on the gpu-pool for mid-length requests (seq 256-512). root cause looks like path-chooser preferring fused-attn-v2 for those batches, but the launch overhead + cont-batching mix is killing tail.

alex: sample selection trace from a hot request: 
```
[2025-11-02T09:12:11Z] seq_len=320 -> candidate_kernels=[fused-attn-v2(estimated=18.3ms), legacy-attn(estimated=12.1ms)]
[decision] chosen=fused-attn-v2 score=0.78 launch_penalty=5.2 batching_gain=1.1
[kv] kv_warm_hit=false kv_warm_rate=0.38
```

alex: note kv_warm_rate was ~0.65 on the previous canary. now it's ~0.35 in production for the same traffic slice. suspect the path change is causing more KV cold paths + smaller effective batch packing. :eyes:

jia: can you attach the pprof link and the autotune config you rolled? want to see the scoring weights.

alex: pprof: https://pprof.internal/redwood/2254/pprof/heap (perm restricted). autotune config snippet: 
```
path_selector: 
  - name: latency_core
    weight: 0.7
  - name: launch_penalty
    weight: 0.25
  - name: kv_affinity
    weight: 0.05
hysteresis_ms: 20
```

omar: tolerate that the fused kernel has better steady-state throughput for long seqs, but higher absolute launch cost. continuous batching will try to combine short/medium requests into a block that tricks the estimator into preferring fused. if kv gets cold during that handoff it amplifies the tail.

lina: can we add a short-circuit rule: for seq in [128..512] prefer legacy-attn unless fused shows sustained >10% win for 5m? basically an override/hardpin.

omar: also look at the batching window config — our cont-batcher has an aggressive shape that mixes 64/320 sequences. reducing max_pack_seq_delta might help.

ajia: i can run an ablation on the scoring weights. if we increase kv_affinity weight from 0.05 -> 0.25 we might favor paths that keep KV warm. that's a quick canary.

alex: repro command I used: 
```bash
INFER_LOAD=sim-mix ./bench/simulate_traffic --dist "mix:{p(64)=0.45,p(320)=0.35,p(1024)=0.2}" --autotune-endpoint $AUTOTUNE
```
results: p95 +12% when path_selector weight unchanged; p95 -6% when i manually pinned legacy for 256-512.

perf-bot: deploy detected: autotune-service v1.8.3 -> v1.9.0 at 2254120000 (author: infra-cd).

omar: that explains it — v1.9 bumped the fused kernel scoring to favor batch efficiency more aggressively. regression plausible.

lina: i'm going to try a quick canary with: 
```json
{"autotune": {"weights": {"kv_affinity": 0.25, "launch_penalty": 0.35}}}
```
and a pinned override for seq 256-512 -> legacy-attn. will post numbers in ~30m.

ajia: i'll prepare a bisect patch to revert only the fused-weight tweak so we can validate. if lina's canary looks good we can ship rollback for prod.

alex: thanks — i'll open an issue with pprof dumps and attach the bench repro + the selection traces. added labels: regression, perf, autotune.

lina: quick update — after 25m canary: p95 down ~8% on the slice, kv_warm_rate climbed to 0.61. looks promising.

omar: nice. follow-up: we should add a synthetic test in CI that simulates mixed seq distributions and asserts no >5% p95 regression on kernel selector changes.

ajia: agreed. i'll draft the CI test and the bisect PR.

alex: perfect. if anyone sees other oddities (esp region-wide), ping me. i'll keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
